entries.evidence: Confirmed dynamically three times over: ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of 910 bytes past the 1032-byte wbuf at src/handlers.c:617 (retained replay), 600 bytes at handlers.c:336 (session resume) and 600 bytes at server.c:354 (inflight retransmit); reproduced at 1 MB (WRITE 3010) and the shipped 50 MB (WRITE 1048587); plain -O3 build exits SIGSEGV (-11) while a one-tuple control survives; gdb proves the overflow bytes are the attacker payload at wbuf+908. Filed as vuln-0001 with inline fixes for all 14 append sites, verified by re-running every PoC plus duplicate-tuple and near-exact-fit bypass variants, smoke test 7/7 and unit tests 13/13 on a patched copy.

entries.surface: UNSUBSCRIBE decode + dispatch (mqtt.c:369-410 unpack_mqtt_unsubscribe, handlers.c:646-679, server.c:868-894)
entries.risk_area: Double free / use-after-free of the decoded packet (memory safety, pre-auth DoS)
entries.evidence: Reproduced with a 7-byte pre-auth packet a2 05 00 01 00 01 41. ASan: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at mqtt.c:585 from process_message server.c:880, freed by mqtt_packet_destroy mqtt.c:586 <- unsubscribe_handler handlers.c:676 (exit -6). Plain build: glibc "free(): double free detected in tcache 2" -> SIGABRT. Control: same-shape SUBSCRIBE 82 06 00 01 00 01 41 00 after CONNECT survives (CONNACK + SUBACK), proving the extra destroy is in unsubscribe_handler. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_unsub_doublefree.py; note d5ff41.

entries.surface: mqtt_unpack dispatch (mqtt.c:72-82 unpack_handlers[11], mqtt.c:422-437) with opcode 11 (UNSUBACK) admitted by server.c:512
entries.risk_area: Out-of-bounds dispatch-table index -> indirect call (pre-auth crash)
entries.evidence: 2-byte pre-auth b0 00. ASan-only build: "global-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 8" at mqtt.c:434, "0 bytes after global variable 'unpack_handlers' ... of size 88". Harness ASan+UBSan build: "index 11 out of bounds for type 'mqtt_unpack_handler *[11]'" at mqtt.c:434 (halts, exit 1). Plain build: SIGSEGV; gdb shows RIP=0 called from process_message server.c:865 with &unpack_handlers[11] = (nil) -- the linker zero after the array. Control b0 02 00 01 (well-formed UNSUBACK) also kills it; c0 00 PINGREQ survives with d0 00. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_unpack_oob_call.py; note bc3c85.

entries.surface: recv_packet framing (server.c:475-575 recv_data/toread vs rbuf allocation at server.c:393-394)
entries.risk_area: Heap buffer overflow by unchecked read length (toread vs rbuf size)
entries.evidence: max_request_size 4096 + a 3-byte length prefix encoding pktlen==4096 (30 80 a0 00 + 4096 bytes): ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4096 at network.c:273 (recv_bytes) <- server.c:575, "0 bytes after 4104-byte region" allocated by client_init server.c:394. gdb trace: recv writes [rbuf+4, rbuf+4100), unpack_bytes copies 4092 bytes from rbuf+8 through rbuf+4099, i.e. the decoder consumes the 4 out-of-bounds bytes. Plain build: glibc "corrupted size vs. prev_size" abort at shutdown. With max_request_size 2 the 4-byte prefix read itself overflows (ASan WRITE of size 2 at server.c:530). Control: pktlen 4092 with 3-byte prefix (toread==4096 exactly) -> no report, PUBLISH decoded (4088 payload). Overrun = pktlen + pos + 1 - max_request_size = pos+1 bytes, max 4 at pktlen==max_request_size. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_toread_overflow.py; note 00e375.

entries.surface: SUBSCRIBE tuple decode + destroy (mqtt.c:324-361 loop counter usize vs u16 tuples_len; mqtt_packet_destroy mqtt.c:582-587)
entries.risk_area: Unbounded memory leak / memory-exhaustion DoS (integer truncation of tuple count)
entries.evidence: 196,618-byte SUBSCRIBE with 65,537 minimal tuples -> SUBACK 90 02 00 01 (tuples_len truncated to 1). LSAN at graceful exit: "Direct leak of 589815 byte(s) in 65535 object(s)" from unpack_bytes pack.c:413 <- unpack_string16 <- unpack_mqtt_subscribe mqtt.c:350 <- process_message server.c:865. Broker-reported $SOL/broker/memory/used grows monotonically +1,114,136 per packet (589,824 real + ~524,296 try_realloc counter drift) and RSS ~+2 MB per packet over 6 packets. The tuples_len==0 variant instead trips handlers.c:545 VLA-bound UBSan first, so 65,537 tuples is used. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_tuple_leak.py; note 013f6d.

entries.surface: CONNECT ClientId overflow, control-flow variant (mqtt.c:235-243 memcpy into client_id[64] inside struct io_event, mqtt.c:568-598 mqtt_packet_destroy)
entries.risk_area: Control-flow hijack via overwritten function pointer in the decoded packet (refcount.free indirect call)
entries.evidence: gdb at connect_handler with cid_len=102 shows username/password/will_topic/will_message holding 0x41../0x42../0x43../0x44.. inside the 144-byte `io` frame. Control that rules the control-flow variant out: mqtt_packet_destroy's CONNECT branch frees only those four pointers and never touches refcount; each free is gated on a flag bit located before the copied region, and with those bits set unpack_mqtt_connect rewrites the pointers with fresh heap allocations (observed 0x7f9d.. values with flags=0xc6); no code path DECREFs a decoded packet (DECREF only on mqtt_packet_alloc copies, handlers.c:755, and i_msgs, handlers.c:93). Aiming refcount.free at 0xdeadbeefcafebabe (cid_len=110) then CONNECT/PINGREQ/PUBLISH/DISCONNECT/close left the broker alive. ASan-only build: silent for cid_len<=117 (overflow stays inside io), reports WRITE of size 1 at mqtt.c:241 for 118 and WRITE of size 130 at mqtt.c:240 for 130. No stack protector: no __stack_chk_fail/__stack_chk_guard and zero fs:0x28 loads in both harness binaries. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_cid_refcount.py; note fd300c.

entries.surface: src/mqtt.c unpack_mqtt_subscribe / unpack_mqtt_unsubscribe tuple loops
entries.risk_area: Integer underflow, unbounded loop/allocation, out-of-bounds read, pre-auth DoS
entries.evidence: Reproduced with 7 bytes (82 05 00 01 00 FF 41 / A2 05 00 01 00 FF 41): production-flags build SIGSEGV in 0.2-0.4 s in unpack_integer via unpack_string16 with len=18446744073707446302; ASan 4 KiB heap-buffer-overflow READ at pack.c:91; ASan 1 MiB RSS 52->965 MB in 0.5 s at ~95% CPU, SIGTERM ignored. Filed as vuln-0005 with inline fixes; patched build survives (flat RSS, no report, rejects packet) and the smoke/functional tests still pass.

entries.surface: src/server.c recv_packet framing and src/mqtt.c mqtt_decode_length
entries.risk_area: Out-of-bounds heap write via unbounded length-prefix decode and unchecked toread, pre-auth
entries.evidence: gdb at server.c:575 on the uninstrumented build shows toread=69537 against a 65536-byte rbuf (4001 bytes past), and toread=1048581 against 1048576. ASan: WRITE of size 69533 at recv from server.c:575; READ of size 1 at mqtt.c:145 for the unbounded walk. Filed as vuln-0006 with inline fixes; patched build survives all six variant/config combinations with no sanitizer report, while 1/2/3-byte Remaining Length packets and a max-sized frame still work.

gaps.surface: src/mqtt.c unpack_mqtt_connect (ClientId copy, will/username/password)
gaps.risk_area: Decoder memory safety — attacker-controlled length driving memcpy
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE, needs dynamic reproduction. mqtt.c:240 memcpy(client_id, buf, cid_len) with cid_len a raw u16 from the wire into u8 client_id[64] (mqtt.h:181) that lives in the stack-resident io.data (server.c:860). No bounds check anywhere; `len` param unused. PoC bytes recorded in note 5243eb (303-byte CONNECT, cid_len=0x0100). Nearest case: ASAN stack-buffer-overflow WRITE; production: stack smashing/control-flow overwrite. Highest-value candidate on target.</evidence>

gaps.surface: src/mqtt.c unpack_mqtt_publish (payloadlen arithmetic)
gaps.risk_area: Decoder memory safety — unsigned underflow to allocation/memcpy size
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE. mqtt.c:314 len -= (2 + topiclen) on usize with no check that 2+topiclen <= len; mqtt.c:316 unpack_bytes(&buf, len) -> pack.c:413 try_alloc(len+1) + pack.c:414 memcpy(dest,*buf,len). len == SIZE_MAX makes try_alloc(0) succeed and memcpy(SIZE_MAX) fault; other magnitudes make malloc fail -> exit(EXIT_FAILURE) (memory.c:49-53). 7-byte PoC `30 05 00 04 41 41 41` (and `30 05 00 FF 41 41 41` for the exit variant) in note 1cc769.</evidence>

gaps.surface: src/mqtt.c unpack_mqtt_subscribe (tuple loop)
gaps.risk_area: Decoder memory safety — unsigned underflow / loop termination / unbounded allocation
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE. mqtt.c:342-358: `for (; len > 0; ++i)` with `len -= sizeof(u16)` at :344 and `len -= topic_len` at :355 on a usize, both before any lower-bound test -> underflow to ~2^64 -> loop never terminates; each iteration reallocs the tuple array, allocates topic_len+1 bytes and copies from a monotonically advancing buf (unbounded OOB heap read). 7-byte PoC `82 05 00 01 00 FF 41` in note 1076b3. Also u16 tuples_len truncation leaks topics past 65536 (note bb1d02).

gaps.surface: src/mqtt.c unpack_mqtt_unsubscribe (tuple loop) + its destroy path
gaps.risk_area: Decoder memory safety — underflow, infinite loop, double free
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE, two distinct defects: (1) same `len -= 2` / `len -= topic_len` underflow as decode before the `len > 0` test (mqtt.c:386-401) -> infinite loop with unbounded OOB reads (note 1076b3, 7-byte PoC `A2 05 00 01 00 FF 41`); (2) double free — handlers.c:676 destroys e->data and server.c:880 destroys io.data again, so the decoded tuples array and each topic are freed twice (note 96c97e, 7-byte PoC `A2 05 00 01 00 01 41` -> glibc abort).

gaps.surface: src/server.c process_message + handle_command
gaps.risk_area: Dispatch of partially decoded packets / error handling
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE: server.c:865 discards mqtt_unpack's return value and server.c:867 dispatches regardless, so handlers act on partially decoded packets (safe only because io.data is zero-initialised at server.c:860). Enables/amplifies the decoder findings and means error returns cannot be relied on for a fix (note 392a40... see note 5243eb family; D9 note id in 'Decoder audit' methodology note). No independent memory-safety consequence found here.

gaps.surface: src/server.c recv_packet (WAITING_HEADER/WAITING_LENGTH/WAITING_DATA) + read_data + mqtt_decode_length call site
gaps.risk_area: Framing/arithmetic — remaining-length decoding, buffer bookkeeping, OOB read/write
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE, two defects: (1) mqtt_decode_length (mqtt.c:136-153) has no MAX_LEN_BYTES cap even though the constant exists at mqtt.c:59 (used only by the encoder) — it is handed rbuf+1 after only 4 bytes were recv'd (server.c:530/545), so continuation bytes at rbuf[4..] (stale previous-packet bytes; rbuf is never scrubbed) drive it past the 512KB allocation (note 3c15c0). (2) server.c:551 validates pktlen but server.c:562 sets toread = pktlen+pos+1 and server.c:575 recv's toread-read bytes into rbuf+read, so pktlen == max_request_size overflows rbuf by pos bytes (4 with the default 512KB config, note e49831). Opcode gate bypass (R1) and pktlen 64->32 truncation (R2) were examined and ruled out in note fb95db.

gaps.surface: src/handlers.c publish_handler + publish_message
gaps.risk_area: Consumption of decoded topic/payload fields (VLA sizing, wbuf writes, retained store)
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE. handlers.c:696-706: `char topic[p->topiclen+2]` VLA then `p->topic[p->topiclen-1]` -> index -1 when topiclen==0 (heap read inside the try_alloc size header, ASAN-invisible); handlers.c:746-749 stores a full serialized copy of the attacker PUBLISH as the retained message, which is the primitive for the wbuf overflow. Payload bytes / payloadlen reach pack_mqtt_publish (mqtt.c:520) via publish_message (handlers.c:227). See note 99b93f (D11) and 392a40-adjacent D10 note.

gaps.surface: src/handlers.c subscribe_handler (rcs/topic VLAs, retained-message copy)
gaps.risk_area: Consumption of decoded tuple fields (VLA sizing, index underflow, wbuf write)
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE. handlers.c:545 `unsigned char rcs[s->tuples_len]` and handlers.c:557-569 `char topic[topic_len+2]` are attacker-sized VLAs (up to 64KB each, ~128KB of stack per handler call) and handlers.c:563/564 index topic[-1]/[-2] when topic_len is 0 or 1 (stack-buffer-underflow READ, 7-byte PoC `82 05 00 01 00 00 02`, note 392a40). handlers.c:615-619 copies each topic's retained message into c->wbuf + c->towrite with no boundary check, once per tuple including duplicates, giving a controlled heap overflow on the 512KB wbuf and a subsequent heap read-back through send_data (note 99b93f).

gaps.surface: src/handlers.c unsubscribe_handler (destroy + REPLY return)
gaps.risk_area: Decoded-object lifetime — double free
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED BY TRACE (note 96c97e): handlers.c:676 mqtt_packet_destroy(&e->data) followed by server.c:880 mqtt_packet_destroy(&io.data) frees the same decoded tuples array and every topic pointer twice; reachable pre-auth with `A2 05 00 01 00 01 41`. Expected ASAN double-free / glibc "double free detected in tcache 2" abort.

gaps.surface: src/bst.c AVL rotate/insert used as the trie child index
gaps.risk_area: Memory safety in topic-trie balancing (NULL deref, broken invariant)
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: bst_rotate_left (bst.c:61-73) reads x->left and then y->right with no NULL check; called from bst.c:139-140 for right-heavy nodes. Three publishes/subscription tuples with ascending first chars (a/x, b/x, c/x) reach NULL deref. Not yet filed; needs dynamic PoC.

gaps.surface: CONNECT handler session table (handlers.c:382-430) + server.sessions uthash
gaps.risk_area: ClientId session takeover / use-after-free on session refcount
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: session reuse branch (handlers.c:400-405) takes no INCREF, only the create branch does (handlers.c:417-419); two clients sharing one ClientId leave refcount 1, and the clean_session=1 client's disconnect DECREFs to 0 and frees the session still pointed at by the other live client (server.c:438). Needs dynamic heap/UAF confirmation.

gaps.surface: src/server.c client_deactivate / client_init lifecycle
gaps.risk_area: Resource leak and lock-state handling on disconnect
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: all teardown is inside if (client->clean_session == true) (server.c:430-443), so a clean_session=false disconnect leaks the struct client plus rbuf/wbuf (2x max_request_size; 100MB with shipped conf) and leaves it in clients_map; max_memory is never enforced (only parsed/printed) and try_alloc exit()s on OOM. Also server.c:415-419 returns with client->mutex held and 442 frees the pool block before the unlock/destroy at 450-451.

gaps.surface: in-flight QoS bookkeeping: handlers.c puback/pubrec/pubcomp/pubrel + server.c inflight_msg_check
gaps.risk_area: Packet-id validation, refcount deref, unbounded retransmit writes
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: inflight_msg_clear on an unused id DECREFs a NULL packet (handlers.c:793, 848 -> ref.h:50-54 writes through NULL); --inflights wraps u16 to 65535 permanently enabling has_inflight; inflight_msg_check re-packs every unacked msg each second into c->wbuf with no bound (server.c:326-359) and its ACK branch packs the stale/NULL p (server.c:354).

gaps.surface: per-client write buffer (wbuf/towrite) across handlers.c publish+subscribe and server.c set_connack/inflight
gaps.risk_area: Unbounded write into fixed-size heap buffer (heap overflow)
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: no site compares towrite against conf->max_request_size; sinks are handlers.c:227, handlers.c:615-619 (retained memcpy), server.c:132-143 (session-resume flush, carries a TODO admitting the missing check), server.c:338/354. Deterministic trigger: two retained messages of S bytes + one SUBSCRIBE with both tuples, 2S+6 > wbuf.

gaps.surface: pre-CONNECT packet processing (server.c:858-898 process_message) and CONNECT credential check (handlers.c:366-374, util.c:142)
gaps.risk_area: Authentication/authorization bypass
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: process_message dispatches every opcode with no connected/auth gate, so with allow_anonymous=false a socket that never sends CONNECT can PUBLISH (handlers.c:681-783 never touches c->session) and set retained messages; bad_auth (handlers.c:482-487) leaves the socket open for unlimited retries. CONNECT itself has no omission bypass (both username and password flags required).

gaps.surface: src/topic.c + src/trie.c + src/topic_store.c subscription/topic store (insert, remove, wildcard fan-out)
gaps.risk_area: Subscription lifecycle and wildcard matching correctness
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: wildcard fan-out guard is inverted (handlers.c:719 iterates only when the list is empty) so '+' filters never deliver and '#' only sees topics existing at subscribe time; UNSUBSCRIBE looks up the unnormalized name (handlers.c:658-663) while subscribe/publish append '/' (handlers.c:567-570, 703-706) so unsubscribing is a no-op; retained_msg replaced without free (handlers.c:747); topic_add_subscriber leaks on duplicate (topic.c:92-96).

gaps.surface: $SOL system topics as a publish target (publish_handler topic handling)
gaps.risk_area: Integrity of broker telemetry topics
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: publish_handler applies no namespace restriction, so any client (even pre-CONNECT) can publish or retain to $SOL/broker/... and poison what other clients read as broker statistics. Low-severity integrity issue; needs dynamic confirmation of the observable effect.

gaps.surface: src/network.c TLS setup (SSL_CTX options, verify mode, handshake)
gaps.risk_area: TLS protocol strength / client authentication
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: SSL_CTX_set_verify(SSL_VERIFY_NONE) at network.c:373 means client certs are never requested, so cafile is inert and mTLS cannot be used as an auth control; protocol gating is negative-option only (network.c:324-338) and the shipped conf enables tlsv1/tlsv1_1; ssl_accept (network.c:393-401) does a single SSL_accept on a non-blocking fd with no WANT_READ retry and returns the SSL* regardless of failure.

gaps.surface: retained message store (struct topic.retained_msg, handlers.c:256-261 / 746-749 / 615-619)
gaps.risk_area: Retained-message ownership, replacement and unbounded growth
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: each retained publish overwrites t->retained_msg without freeing the previous buffer (handlers.c:747) and the LWT path does the same (handlers.c:259-261); no cap on retained size or topic count; the buffer is replayed into a subscriber's fixed wbuf with only alloc_size as the length (handlers.c:615-619), which is the write-buffer overflow trigger. Owners: topic (freed only by topic_destroy, which never runs at runtime).

gaps.surface: SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE/PLC topic string indexing (handlers.c:557-570, 696-706)
gaps.risk_area: Out-of-bounds read on attacker-supplied topic length
gaps.detail: Confirmed by trace: VLA char topic[tuple_len+2] with u16 tuple_len, then topic[tuple_len-1] and topic[tuple_len-2] (handlers.c:563-564,567) - for length 0/1 these are topic[-1]/topic[-2]; same class at handlers.c:703 (p->topic[p->topiclen-1] with topiclen 0). Reads only, used in comparisons, so impact is low but the access is out of bounds. Needs a 1-byte dynamic check (ASAN build).

gaps.surface: Reuse of the freed client_session chunk with attacker-controlled PUBLISH payload (session UAF exploitation)
gaps.risk_area: Controlled reallocation of freed session memory (UAF -> attacker bytes)
gaps.detail: Size classes match (sizeof(client_session)=320, try_alloc header 8 -> 328-byte malloc request; a retained PUBLISH packed to 320 bytes issues the same 328-byte request), but /workspace/poc/poc_session_reuse.sh (gdb, non-ASan build) still shows the original "victim" bytes when subscriber_new copies session->session_id, i.e. the freed chunk was not reclaimed. The free and the later allocation land on different event-loop threads (THREADSNR 2 + main loop all epoll one listener), so the chunk stays in another thread's tcache; ASan quarantine blocks the experiment there. Not demonstrated; would need thread placement control or tcache-draining grooming.

gaps.surface: Pre-CONNECT PUBLISH against allow_anonymous=false broker (src/server.c process_message -> handlers.c publish_handler)
gaps.risk_area: Authentication bypass / unauthorized publish and retained-message injection
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED, report not filed here. No connected/authenticated gate in process_message or publish_handler. Anonymous socket PUBLISH (0x31 retain=1) accepted with no error; QoS1 publish answered `40 07 07` (PUBACK); retained payload from the anonymous socket delivered to an authenticated subscriber (`31 00 0b ... | 90 00 01 00`); anonymous retain overwrote TRUSTED-ORIGINAL with FORGED-BY-ANON for both the live subscriber and later subscribers. Control: same publish after valid CONNECT behaves identically. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_preauth_publish.py, evidence /workspace/poc/evidence/02_preauth_authz.txt.

gaps.surface: Pre-CONNECT SUBSCRIBE (src/handlers.c subscribe_handler, line 589 topic_add_subscriber)
gaps.risk_area: Pre-auth NULL dereference DoS (unauthenticated SUBSCRIBE)
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED, report not filed here. subscribe_handler has no connected check; topic_add_subscriber -> subscriber_new (src/subscriber.c:45) memcpy's from the NULL client->session. Pre-CONNECT `82 10 00 01 00 0b plv/preauth 00` gives PEER-CLOSED and UBsan "member access within null pointer of type 'struct client_session'" (subscriber.c:45 -> topic.c:92 -> handlers.c:588); dev build SIGSEGV, also in the default allow_anonymous=true config. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_preauth_publish.py unauth-subscribe, evidence /workspace/poc/evidence/02_preauth_authz.txt.

gaps.surface: Session teardown for clean_session=false clients (src/server.c client_deactivate, lines 411-451)
gaps.risk_area: Unbounded memory growth / remote resource-exhaustion DoS
gaps.detail: CONFIRMED, report not filed here. client_deactivate (server.c:430-443) frees the client/session only when clean_session==true. Measured on the dev build (max_request_size 1MB): 40 cycles clean_session=1 plateau at +6156 KiB total (0 KiB/cycle from cycle ~15); 40 cycles clean_session=0 with unique ClientId grow +155664 KiB = 3891.6 KiB/connection, linear (VmRSS 54 MB -> 210 MB). Decomposition: same ClientId + DISCONNECT = 2048-2253 KiB/cycle (the two max_request_size buffers), so the per-session tables (i_acks 512 KiB + i_msgs ~1.5 MiB) add ~1.6 MiB. Under RLIMIT_AS=700MB the broker exits after 127 connections: "memory.c:51 Out of memory (1048576 bytes)", status 1. PoC /workspace/poc/poc_session_leak.py, evidence /workspace/poc/evidence/04_session_leak.txt.

gaps.surface: CONNECT authentication failure path (bad_auth, src/handlers.c:483-487) with allow_anonymous=false
gaps.risk_area: Credential brute force / no rate limiting or lockout
gaps.detail: Measured: 4 wrong-password CONNECTs on one socket each answered `20 00 04` with the socket kept open, then a retained PUBLISH from that never-authenticated socket was accepted and delivered to an authenticated subscriber, then a correct-password CONNECT on the same socket was accepted (`20 00 00`). No delay, lockout, connection close, or attempt counter exists in the bad_auth path (handlers.c:482-487) — only the cost of one SHA-512-crypt verification per attempt limits throughput. Supporting weakness for the auth-bypass finding; low severity on its own. Evidence /workspace/poc/evidence/02_preauth_authz.txt.

gaps.surface: Operator config max_memory (src/config.c:228, src/server.c:236)
gaps.risk_area: Configured resource limit not enforced
gaps.detail: Confirmed by source and by measurement: max_memory is parsed (config.c:228-229) and only read back for the $SOL stats payload (server.c:236 memory_used()); no allocation path consults it. A broker configured with max_memory 8MB kept running at 87 MB VmRSS after 10 clean_session=0 connections (10x over the cap) and only died when RLIMIT_AS made malloc fail (memory.c:51 exit). Recorded as a supporting fact for the memory-exhaustion finding, not as an independent vulnerability.

gaps.surface: check_passwd() empty stored hash / strncasecmp hash comparison (src/util.c:142)
gaps.risk_area: Fail-open credential comparison
gaps.detail: Confirmed: with a password_file entry `emptyuser:` (empty hash field) any password is accepted - arbitrary, empty and 60-char passwords all returned CONNACK rc=0 while the control user alice still returned rc=4. Cause: strlen(salt)==0 makes strncasecmp(...,0)==0. Confirmed but NOT filed as a report (task instruction); parent should decide reporting. Severity: low - requires an operator-written password file with an empty hash field.

gaps.surface: Repeated CONNECT on a single socket after rc=4 (server.c process_message re-arm path)
gaps.risk_area: Credential brute force / missing rate limiting
gaps.detail: Confirmed: after rc=4 the broker neither closes the socket nor slows down. 2157 CONNECT attempts with wrong passwords on ONE TCP socket in 5.00s = 431.2 attempts/s (all rc=4), and a correct password on that same socket afterwards still returned rc=0. No lockout, backoff or disconnect exists (handlers.c returns MQTT_BAD_USERNAME_OR_PASSWORD and server.c just enqueues the CONNACK and re-arms EV_READ). Not filed as a report per task instruction; parent should decide (medium: offline-dictionary-speed online guessing per connection, scales with connection count).

gaps.surface: Username lookup timing in connect_handler (known vs unknown user)
gaps.risk_area: Username enumeration via response-time oracle
gaps.detail: Confirmed oracle: 150 CONNECTs per case. Known username 'alice' mean 2.39 ms / median 2.19 ms / p95 3.62 ms; unknown username mean 0.14 ms / median 0.09 ms / p95 0.20 ms - 17x with no overlap, because `if (!auth || !check_passwd(...))` only runs crypt() when the username exists. Confirmed but not filed per task instruction; feeds the brute-force item (attacker learns valid usernames, then guesses at 431/s per socket).

gaps.surface: check_passwd()/crypt(3) under concurrent authentication (src/util.c:142, 3 event-loop threads)
gaps.risk_area: Data race in credential verification (wrong accept/reject)
gaps.detail: Confirmed false rejects, no false accepts. Library level: libcrypt 4.5.2 crypt() called from 3 threads with one salt produced 3340 wrong results out of 3352 calls (0/900 wrong serially). Broker level: serial control 60/60 good accepted and 60/60 bad rejected; with 4 concurrent clients 2063/2140 correct-password attempts got CONNACK rc=4 and 0/2138 wrong-password attempts were accepted; second run (8 workers, 90 s) 21558/22508 legit rejected, 0/22883 wrong-password accepts. Root cause: sol calls non-reentrant crypt() from 3 event loops with no lock (util.c:142-145, handlers.c). Impact is authentication DoS / lockout of a known account, not bypass. Not filed per task instruction.

gaps.surface: TLS data path ssl_recv_bytes() (src/network.c:438-455)
gaps.risk_area: Pre-authentication denial of service (busy loop)
gaps.detail: Confirmed pre-auth CPU exhaustion, no credentials needed: one TLS connection that sends a 3-byte truncated record (`16 03 01`) and stays silent pins a worker thread in ssl_recv_bytes()'s `continue` on SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ. LD_PRELOAD counter on SSL_read shows ~800,000 calls/second (777451, 865766, 869275, 847659, 800826, 789077, 719399, 898729). One connection = 74-86% of a core; 3 connections (one per event loop, THREADSNR=2+main) = ~200% CPU with per-thread ticks 857/790/969, and a legitimate TLS client then cannot complete a handshake (8 s timeout). Not filed per task instruction; this is the highest-impact item found (A:H, AV:N, PR:N).

gaps.surface: tls_protocols policy (src/config.c:191-265, conf/sol.conf) and protocol negotiation
gaps.risk_area: Weak TLS protocol versions enabled by shipped configuration
gaps.detail: Observed with openssl s_client against a broker using the shipped protocol list: TLSv1 ACCEPTED (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA), TLSv1.1 ACCEPTED, TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 ACCEPTED; TLSv1.0 succeeded even at s_client's default security level, so the server really offers it. `tls_protocols tlsv1_2` correctly rejected 1.0/1.1/1.3. Default when the directive is omitted is TLSv1.2 only (TLSv1.3 rejected because `#ifdef TLS1_3_VERSION` is false while compiling config.h). Weak/insecure default rather than an exploitable flaw; not filed per task instruction.

gaps.surface: max_request_size buffer allocation per client (src/server.c:client_init, shipped conf 50MB)
gaps.risk_area: Memory exhaustion denial of service (per-connection buffer cost)
gaps.detail: Confirmed: try_calloc is malloc+memset so both per-client buffers are resident immediately. With `max_request_size 50MB` 20 idle TCP connections (no bytes, no credentials) took RSS from 76 MB to 2145 MB = ~107 MB/connection, retained after all closed; with 1MB the same test is ~2 MB/connection. max_memory is never enforced and try_alloc exits on failure (memory.c:49-53): under an 800 MB address-space cap the broker died at the 8th connection, "Out of memory (52428800 bytes)", exit status 1. Not filed per task instruction; availability impact for the shipped 50MB config.

gaps.surface: Rejected CONNECT followed by SUBSCRIBE on the same socket (handlers.c:588 subscriber_new)
gaps.risk_area: Processing of MQTT commands by an unauthenticated peer (crash)
gaps.detail: Confirmed with the ASan build: CONNECT with a wrong password returns CONNACK rc=4, then the same socket can send SUBSCRIBE and the broker dispatches it - subscriber_new (src/subscriber.c:45) dereferences a NULL client_session ("runtime error: member access within null pointer of type 'struct client_session'") and the broker aborts. Two small packets, no credentials, pre-auth denial of service. This sits on the boundary with the pre-CONNECT/dispatch area another agent owns, so it is recorded here for the parent to route/dedupe rather than filed.

gaps.surface: Shipped conf/sol.conf security posture
gaps.risk_area: Insecure shipped defaults (no auth, legacy TLS, oversized buffers)
gaps.detail: Confirmed posture, three parts: (1) allow_anonymous is commented out in conf/sol.conf and the compiled default is true, so the shipped deployment is unauthenticated; (2) the shipped tls_protocols value enables TLS 1.0 and 1.1 (verified accepted) alongside 1.2/1.3; (3) max_request_size 50MB costs ~107 MB RSS per idle connection and exhaustion kills the process. The broker also refuses to start as shipped because certs/ca.crt is absent (fail-closed, exit 1), so the TLS defaults only apply once an operator supplies certificates. Recorded as an insecure-default observation, not an exploitable flaw.

gaps.surface: Embedded NUL bytes in CONNECT username/password (unpack_string16, mqtt.c:251-257)
gaps.risk_area: Credential string confusion (embedded NUL)
gaps.detail: Confirmed: username `alice\0junk` with the correct password returned rc=0 (C-string truncation in the uthash lookup), and passwords `secret123\0junk` / `secret123\0` also returned rc=0 (crypt stops at NUL). MQTT 3.1.1 requires UTF-8 strings without U+0000, which sol never validates. Low on its own - the same credential is reached by a shorter string - but it is a second credential representation that any auditing/provisioning component would treat differently.
